sections.name: I. Receding Peaks, and Garlic
sections.overview:
Dobbs sat by the cracked chin-bubble and watched Mount Ebot shrink. One T. The peak that had taken a night, a scalp, and a tail boom was already a grey knuckle in rain.

The cabin still smelled of onion sack and wet wool. The rotor beat through the floorboards. The charter pilot's hands were on the stick; they were not steady.

Wario let out a rattling sigh that made the seat complain. He found a squashed clove in his belt pouch and bit it. The crunch was the first cheerful sound since the cairn.

"Yeah," he said. "It's a real sight." The bite was gone from his voice. "That hill was a waste. Headache and a busted machine." He chuckled anyway. "We ain't done. When we find it, I'm the one with the biggest pile. Don't fall asleep on me."

He shut his eyes. His ears stayed open for the pilot.

Waluigi had his face on the cold glass. Snow-caps went to specks. His limbs did not fit the seat.

"Don't act like a hero, Jory." His voice cracked over the rotors. "If you hadn't been so *loud* with the punching, I wouldn't have had to lift the wiring." He turned on Wario. "And you. Stop being the boss. I kept this bucket in the air. Without me you'd still be down there letting that man nap until he froze."

He crossed his arms. "When we get the treasure I take a bigger cut. I'm tired of the work while he sits there looking *large*."

Dobbs pulled the tattered cloak tighter and asked how long the trip was.

"Who knows?" Waluigi snapped. "Shortcuts. The pilot is reading a map in a mirror. Fumes and good vibes. More than a few hours and I get cranky. Stay awake. I will not shake you at every bump."

From the front, Wario, eyes still shut: "Keep the bird moving. I'm hungry for more than garlic."
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi was in this room. He wants that stated, because Part I had to reconstruct the villa from other people's mouths. The glass was cold. The clove was real. The cut argument started before anyone had counted the crates.

sections.name: II. Anyone Coming to the Bin
sections.overview:
Dobbs stood up. The cloak snagged a rivet and came free. "Spare parts bin. Maybe there's something. Anyone coming."

Wario's eyes opened so fast his mustache jumped. "Now you're talking." The rest of the clove went in. He pointed a thick finger at the cramped alcove aft of the seats — plastic crates, a flicker bulb, the smell of old grease that had been in the machine since before the storm.

"I saw it when we loaded. Scrap means loot. Copper. Gears. Or parts so this junk stops dying. I'm going. If it's shiny I'm taking it." His boots hit the floorboards like unpaid invoices.

Waluigi unfolded with a pop of joints. "Obviously." He wiped grease off his chin with a tarnished handkerchief. "I'm not letting that lug hoard. Fairly divided. And if there are actual spare parts, maybe the rattling stops. My ears are ringing. Lead the way. Gold-plated gear is mine."

The alcove was as advertised: rusted gears, jagged plate, hydraulic pistons in weathered crates, one bulb doing its best. Oxidation sat on the tongue.

Dobbs put the rusted iron dagger to the first lid. The edge was notched. The crate was the same metal, only thicker.

The blade caught. Orange-red flake exploded. It coated the cloak, the pistons, Waluigi's handkerchief. The dagger stuck. The sound was a dull clink, not a shing.

Waluigi covered his ears. "A banshee with a chest cold! You are prying with dumpster iron. Move aside."

Dobbs moved aside.

Wario laughed until the bulb flickered. "Chocolate teapot." He did not use the dagger. He planted his feet, took the lid in both hands, and heaved. The hinges screamed. The lid hit the wall. *CRACK.*

"Give me something shiny."
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* The hire opened a Wario crate with a Wario dagger and was surprised when both objects agreed to be rust. Waluigi has opened jars with less theatre and more success.

sections.name: III. Pocket Change and Heavy Hitters
sections.imageCaption: First crate, lid off. Steel gear with an oily sheen at the bottom; Dobbs' brass coin already palmed. The bulb is the only witness that does not shout.
sections.overview:
Dobbs picked through the scatter while Wario mined. A jagged scrap of oxidized iron. A dull brass coin, emblem gone. He palmed both and looked at what the large man had decided was the venture.

Wario's hand closed on weight. He pulled up a heavy industrial gear — teeth still sharp, steel still holding an oily sheen under the grime — and a rectangular block of lead and brass that had come out of something expensive.

"Not junk. Collectors. Or we overhaul the lawnmower." He glanced at Dobbs' coin. "Pocket change. Wahaha."

Dobbs turned the coin once. "It was in the cargo hold. You packed it. How else does it get on the Wariocopter. Did we haul these without opening them."

Wario froze. The grin slipped. His eyes went crate, gear, Dobbs, wall.

"I— uh." Gravel in the throat. "A man of my stature does not dump things. System. Meticulous. Essential. Logistics. Weight. Aerodynamics. The shiny-factor. These were the best parts."

The laugh wheezed.

He leaned in. "Don't get philosophical. They're on the plane. Our loot. Packed or acquired — same result. Help me price them."

Dobbs looked at the unopened barrels. "All right. A system. You open. You give out what you think is useful."

Wario's shoulders dropped, then inflated. "Fine. I can do organized. Master of Goods. You watch for surprises. I lift. I think. Streamlined." He grabbed the next crate. "Prepare for distribution."
sections.waluigi_note: Dobbs asked the only question that matters on a charter you loaded yourself: who put the treasure in the treasure hunt. Wario answered with aerodynamics. Waluigi files that as a confession with extra syllables.

sections.name: IV. The Wario-System
sections.overview:
The second crate was wood and rusted bands. Wario shoved it to the centre. Dust. He came up with a soot-covered industrial wrench, notched head, built for work that leaves marks.

"You. Swinging. Unscrewing. Tool of the trade." He tossed it. Dobbs caught the weight against his chest.

Wario's face lit on a small leather pouch that sat heavy, and a coil of high-tensile wire. Both went into his own belt.

"Strategic supplies. Emergency weight management."

Waluigi had been on the bulkhead the whole time. He pushed off. His shadow cut the scrap into long pieces.

"Bravo. A system. Charity for the delusional. He gives you the lifting and keeps the steal-later. You are his mule. Do not let the voice fool you."

He ignored the wrench. He pointed into a corner Wario had not emptied: a small silver canister, pressurized, light enough for a pocket.

"If you want to be useful, take that. Coolant. Lubricant. Worth something when the engine screams. Wario — drop that gear on my toes again and your next meal is unseasoned crackers."

There was a [[prop:prop_ebot_p2_calendar|calendar in the junk]]. Dobbs read it before he moved.

18 Aethel, 1032 BF.

The day after the plank.

He went for the canister.

Wario threw his head back until the mustache touched his chest. "Another expert. Fine. Take the tin. Probably perfume so the pilot doesn't smell like a locker room. Don't spill it on the boots. High-quality leather."

He went back into the crate with both arms.

Waluigi's eyebrows went up, then settled into smug. "A modicum of sense. Don't get comfortable. You're still a liability in a cloak. Wario — stop pulling like a caveman."
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi pointed at the only object in the crate that could still do a job. Wario kept the pouch. The calendar is why this leaf is dated the 18th and not 'the next morning' — Dobbs read the paper, which is more than Wario did with the stencils.

sections.name: V. PROPERTY OF WARIO WARE INC
sections.imageCaption: Brass fitting and frayed data cable, stencil intact. PROPERTY OF WARIO WARE INC. The joke is that the room agrees.
sections.overview:
Waluigi put Dobbs on small metal. "Jewelry of the machine world. Brass. Copper. If it aches the back, Wario can have it. Data cables under that piston — light, stashable. Lazy loaders dump waste on top."

Dobbs opened the next box. Tangled multi-coloured cable, frayed, intact. A brass fitting. He turned the fitting to the bulb.

The stencil was still readable.

[[prop:prop_ebot_warioware_stencil|PROPERTY OF WARIO WARE INC.]]

Wario's neck muscles stood out. He lunged and took the cable in a vice.

"That's-a my property. Secure bin. Not for rummaging. Handling fee." He shook it at Waluigi. "Don't laugh. I know what you're pricing."

Dobbs did not argue the cable. He looked at the rest of the alcove.

Every crate. Every barrel. The same stencil, or a cousin of it. WarioWare. Wario Ware Inc. Property of.

Wario's face went red, then white. He clutched his head. The charter shuddered under his pacing.

"Everything? Inventory like confetti. Guards asleep. Pilot sold it. The kingdom stole it." He stopped. The eyes narrowed. "Wait. If it's all mine we aren't scavenging. We're reclaiming. Corporate audit. Aggressive. Recovery team. Start hauling."

He slung a crate of gears over one shoulder as if the argument had been about weight all along.

Waluigi cackled. "A thief with a better excuse. Tell the authorities 'reclaiming' and they still call it a heist. However." He traced a barrel rim. "The logistics are favourable. We aren't stealing from the kingdom. We are gathering assets. Organize them, you idiot. Electronics together. Heavy scrap back."

Dobbs was already turning toward the seats. "We're in the air. No one is going to check. You or Wario brought it. Pointless. How far to Ebott." Two T. The right mountain. "I'm going to the luxury seating."
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* He labelled his own hold, forgot he had labelled it, and then billed the discovery as an audit. Waluigi has seen better bookkeeping in a sock.

sections.name: VI. The Pilot's Personal Request
sections.overview:
Wario's crate tilted. He set it down with a thud that made the floorboards groan. Relief came out of him like a puncture.

"You're-a right. Hidden route. If no one sees it, it never happened. Perfect crime. Or perfect audit." He stayed with the barrels. "Go sit. I'll make sure no one snoops. Don't sleep. Real lifting later. Distance — I don't know the miles. Profit when we land."

The luxury seating was the part of the charter that still pretended to be a company: velvet that had been crimson once, a low table, the smell of old tobacco trying to cover hydraulic fluid.

The cabin door creaked. The charter pilot leaned on the frame. Grease overalls. He did not look at the crates. He looked at Dobbs.

"Hey, kid. Official, I know. Fuel sensors are acting up. Kingdom tech. I need a steady source for the navigation lights over the mountains. I saw the canister."

Waluigi stood as if he had been invited onto a stage. "Mechanical tantrum. Tragic. I can be a hero for smooth sailing. Official record. I don't work free. Extra attention to cargo safety."

Dobbs cut across him. "I can help. In exchange for money."

The pilot's mouth twitched. One yellow eye — the crash had left him a colour. "Money speaks. I can't give you a treasury. I can leave blind spots on the manifests. Canister to the main terminal. Pressurized. Sync the valve with the auxiliary output. Wrong, and navigation is the least of it."

He put a tarnished brass key on Dobbs' palm. "Maintenance locker. Bypass kit. If Wario asks why the lights stopped flickering, tell him you're optimizing. He'll believe anything that keeps loot safe."

The key was still warm from the overalls pocket.
sections.waluigi_note: The man who flew them into a cave now sells 'blind spots' for a tin of coolant. Waluigi wanted the consultation fee. Dobbs asked for money out loud, which is the only language that has ever worked on this aircraft.

sections.name: VII. Brains, Brawn, Delicate
sections.overview:
Dobbs spun the key. "Waluigi. Split it and come, or stay."

Waluigi was on his feet before the word *split* had finished. "Favourite language. We go. I watch the distribution. Technical consultant. You negotiate."

"Wario is coming too," Dobbs said. "Less money for me. Maintenance room. Cores."

The engine pit was a trench of ozone and grease. Sodium lamps. Oil in rainbow slicks. Hydraulic pistons in the walls. Wario's boots rang on the grating.

"This is work. Dump full of opportunity. Squeeze the pilot. Lead."

Dobbs pointed Waluigi at the locker. The key ground, then turned. Inside: rusted tools, rags, a heavy metal case that hit a crate with a thump.

"Magic kit," Waluigi said. "Wires. Wrenches. I tinker. You lift. Don't let his paws near the wiring."

Dobbs looked at the three of them. "I get it. I'm the brains. Wario is the brawn. You're the… delicate one." He found a folded note in the kit, read it to himself, and tossed it. The goods were a grease-stained rag and a small copper bundle.

Wario's laugh shook the pipes. Gold tooth. "Brains, brawn, delicate. Nice ring. Premium brawn. Move."

The pilot had followed them down. He leaned on a pillar with his arms folded. Cold. "Let's not get ahead of ourselves with the titles."

Dobbs hissed. "If you're just watching, what's the point of us helping you." He took the rag and the wire. He took the key back off the locker door and pocketed it.

Wario went crimson, then delighted. "Feisty. Tell me where to put my weight." He took the copper bundle. The strands groaned.

"Nearly twenty-three," Dobbs said. "Don't get excited." He put the rag to the housing.

The grease went on too thick, or in the wrong place. The contact smeared. The rag tore.

The pilot's yellow eye tracked the hands. "Smart to try. Don't jam it. Heat will seize the gears over the next ridge. Even. Clean contacts, not wet. I am not flying a gorge in the dark."
sections.waluigi_note: Dobbs named the jobs correctly and then failed a rag, which is the most honest sequence in the leaf. The note in the kit was not filed. If it mattered, someone would have kept it. They kept the key.

sections.name: VIII. Fuel Tank A1
sections.imageCaption: Fuel Tank A1: rusted reservoir, iridescent oil, sodium lamps. The silver canister is at the auxiliary valve. The screen is not yet green.
sections.overview:
Dobbs packed the kit. "Fuel tank. This should be everything."

The walk from the industrial landing block to Wario's private dock was a corridor that tasted of burnt oil. Ten minutes. Wario talked the whole way about schedules.

Fuel Tank A1 was a chamber with a rusted steel reservoir slick as a soap bubble and fumes you could chew. Piping. Pressure valves. Sodium lamps making long shadows.

Wario whistled. "A vein of loot. Grime — which valve pays without bringing the ceiling down."

He had started using a name for the pilot. The archive does not. The man in the overalls did not correct him.

"Those aren't handles. Pressure-regulated. Wrong crank, and you wear industrial accident. I check flow first. You." He meant Dobbs. "Brains today. Watch the gauge on that canister while I hook the main line. Needle in the red — you say so before the pipes scream. You" — Wario — "stay back unless you want to be dragged out of a ceiling."

Dobbs stepped to Waluigi and dropped his voice. "What's the point of him paying us if he's helping anyway. Shouldn't the pilot be piloting." Then, to himself, loud enough: "Sync the pressure valve with the auxiliary output. Main terminal." He looked at the screen on the tank.

Waluigi's whisper was a rasp. "He isn't doing a favour. He's a tool Wario is squeezing. He pays so he still feels in charge. He flies just enough that we don't hit a crevasse. Focus on the valve."

The pilot heard the vibration of it. He came off the doorframe. "A lot of noise for the brains. I don't have time for philosophy. Kingdom grid is garbage. Sync it. I want those lights steady."
sections.waluigi_note: Dobbs asked why a paid man was doing the work he had paid for. Waluigi's answer was unkind and accurate. The archive leaves the pilot unnamed; Wario's nickname is not a character page.

sections.name: IX. All Clear
sections.overview:
Dobbs set the canister at the auxiliary fitting as if it might bite. Wario loomed until the panel was all mustache.

"Break it and I dock your pay."

"You're docking my non-existent pay," Dobbs said, and shoved.

A spark. A whine. The screen flickered hard. Wario's knees remembered the cave.

"Hardware! Green before the wind."

Waluigi laughed from a rib of the fuselage. "Let him scream. Left. You're fighting the pressure. Brains, remember."

Dobbs moved a fraction left and read the screen out loud: bar graph, line graph, a red light, a yellow light, a green light, all three lit at once.

He hesitated. "Looks fine. Let's talk payment."

The pilot's jaw tightened. "Fine is not a number. I want the delta on the variance. Hairpin on the line mid-ascent and *fine* is the last word on the mountainside. Payment is between the owner and the muscle. You stick to dials."

Wario and the pilot stepped back. Dobbs spun the calibrations. "Fields within acceptable bounds, wouldn't you say, Purple Stache. Flux is — no. Normal operational range. Sustaining."

"*Wah!* Nicknames." Wario's pat nearly folded him. "If it's acceptable it's Wario-approved. Heartstone. Stay green. Yellow is your repair bill."

Waluigi: "He sees green as go. Watch the variance. I am watching your value."

The pilot slammed a wrench on a pipe. "Enough. Needles in the red, the tank vents. Gauge. Steady."

Dobbs turned dial A1 to B2, C9 to I2, flux flow to twenty percent, industrial mixer on. The lights went green, one after another. A ding.

All clear.

He sighed.

Waluigi squinted at twenty percent as if it were an insult. "A whisper. Better than the next dimension. Not the hero. Grunt work."

Wario's hand on the shoulder was a shove. "Oversized head paying off. Commission when we find the Heartstone. Don't tell Waluigi. Get the bird moving."
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* He called me Purple Stache to my brother's face and then made the tank say All Clear at a whisper. Waluigi will allow the nickname. He will not allow twenty percent to be called heroism.

sections.name: X. Dinner, and the Rift
sections.overview:
They took the long talk back to the cockpit: oil-slick analog, flickering CRTs, wiring in the dash like veins, red warning lights still pulsing out of habit.

Dobbs found the crumpled [[prop:prop_ebot_vip_clearance|VIP clearance]] in his pocket. The pilot pretended not to see it. Dobbs bit the hardened ration. It tasted like the box it came in.

Wario wrinkled his nose. "Sawdust. That paper doesn't make you boss. If it gets us past guards, fine. Security chumps get a corporate statement. I throw them."

The pilot hunched over the nav console. Yellow eye on the altimeter. "Mouth shut. Eyes forward. Chew quietly. Wario — your voice is on the sensors. Hot zone."

Dobbs looked at the map. "Refueling zone. Three days. What's for dinner."

The pilot's laugh had no humour. The housing rang under his hand. "Dinner. You think this is a tour. You think I plate a meal over a dimensional rift. You eat what Wario scavenges. We're on fumes into a dead zone. Heartstone with a side of steak if you must pray. I know the map. Sit down."

Waluigi groaned theatrically. "A grumpy pilot who thinks he's why we aren't pancakes, and a human worried about his tummy. His grump is how he stays in charge. I want treasure, not three days of biscuits."

Dobbs stopped chewing. "Hold up. Dimensional rift. I asked for dinner because I am hungry." The second bite of ration failed him — dry, stuck, eyes watering. "We can't gloss that. Where are we stopping. Game plan. I never heard this."

Waluigi scoffed. "Not a scenic tour. Not our backyard, you thick-headed human. The rift is why the scenery is a fever dream and why this mountain shouldn't be on our maps. Summit. Wario's shiny rock — Heartstone. I keep us from glaciers and cave weirdos while he counts coins that aren't there. Don't choke. He'll treat you as cargo."

"First," Dobbs said, "you say human like you're not one. Second, I'm going to see if there's food in storage. You can handle your little dimensional rifts alone."

Waluigi's face did the offended disbelief. "Excuse me. Masterpiece of biology. Proportions. Not a peasant from your side of the rift. Handle it alone — I'm why this junk isn't a lawn ornament. Go play scavenger hunt. Don't cry when it's cardboard and grease. *Waaaah.*"

Dobbs went aft toward storage. The lights stayed green. The map still said three days. The rift did not get a second sentence from the man flying.
sections.waluigi_note: The hire asked the question the villa briefing skipped: what world is this. Waluigi answered with Heartstone and proportions. The file ends with Dobbs hunting dinner, which is the correct priority when the last honest meal was a wrapped loaf on a crashing floor.

outcome: Airborne. Navigation lights holding on a twenty-percent pulse from a silver canister that was already in Wario's own hold. Wario in possession of a steel gear, a lead-brass block, a heavy pouch, wire, and a legal theory called audit. Dobbs in possession of a wrench, scrap, a dull coin, a brass key, a VIP card, and the knowledge that every stencil in the alcove already said WarioWare. Waluigi in possession of the argument. The charter pilot in possession of the stick and a sentence he had not used on the 17th: dimensional rift. Destination still Mount Ebott, two T. Heartstone unnamed on any chart in the file. Three days to a refuel. Dinner not served.

aftermath: Standing: the party remains three plus one unnamed charter pilot, still unpaid, still pointed at the mountain with two T. Materiel: WarioWare inventory 'reclaimed' in place; canister committed to the auxiliary valve; VIP card in Dobbs' pocket; key in Dobbs' pocket. Exposure: the pilot now speaks of a rift and a Heartstone that were not on the 17th's briefing table. The wrong mountain is behind them. The right one is not yet under the skids.
waluigiAssessment: 1. Wario packed his own company property, forgot, looted it, and renamed the forgetting an audit. The stencil is the finding. 2. Dobbs is the only person on the aircraft who reads labels, calendars, and maps in that order. 3. The silver canister was the only object in the hold still able to do work; Waluigi pointed; Dobbs took it; the lights went green. That is the whole technical plot. 4. The charter pilot is not a new character. He is the same concussed man from Part I, now selling blind spots. Wario's nickname for him is not canon. 5. 'Dimensional rift' and 'Heartstone' enter the file as speech, not as surveyed fact. Recommendation: keep the One-T file open until someone puts a Heartstone on a table that is not Wario's imagination.
